name: Worley Limited
executive_summary: Worley is a globally diversified engineering and project-delivery group serving energy, chemicals and resources markets, with a quantitative screen rating of **buy** on cheapness (P/B ~1.0, FCF yield 9.2%), dividend yield (4.7%) and balance-sheet metrics (D/E 47%). The investment case rests on a large backlog ($16.7bn per HY26 presentation), accelerating bookings (+63% in H1 FY26) and a capital-return programme (25c interim dividend; up to $500m buyback), against a share price that news coverage suggests has lagged over the past year. The central debate is whether resilient **underlying** earnings (flat underlying EBITA at $377m on aggregated revenue up 5% in H1 FY26) and a $100m+ cost-out target from FY27 can offset **statutory** margin compression, repeated FY26 guidance downgrades linked to Middle East disruption and FX, and structurally low reported ROE (6.5%). Full-year primary filing coverage in the research pack is thin — only HY26 interim accounts and a results presentation are indexed — so annual trend analysis relies partly on Yahoo fallback data.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen passes nine of 22 models across all four families (cheapness, dividend, GARP, risk), with composite score 68% and sector-relative 69%, signalling a statistically cheap, income-generating name with acceptable leverage. That aligns with filing evidence of disciplined capital management: leverage 1.5x (target <2.0x), liquidity $2.3bn, normalized cash conversion 95.5%, and an active buyback ($158m in H1 FY26; $324m cumulative to 31 December 2025 per presentation).

Business quality is mixed but not disqualifying for a value investor. Worley’s moat is relationship- and execution-driven: 79% reimbursable contracts, sole-sourced wins at 48%, and diversified exposure across Americas, EMEA and APAC. H1 FY26 aggregated revenue rose 5% to $6,312m; underlying EBITA was essentially flat at $377m; underlying EBITA margin excluding procurement improved to 8.8% (from 8.4%). Backlog of $16.7bn and post-period wins (including >$3.5bn since 1 January 2026 per presentation) support revenue visibility.

The screen’s buy signal is reinforced by tangible book proximity (P/B 1.01), strong FCF generation (Yahoo FY25 operating cash flow $741m; screen FCF ~$497m), and a maintained 25c unfranked interim dividend. The value case is essentially “quality cyclical at trough multiples”: market scepticism after profit warnings may have overshot operational momentum visible in bookings and cost-reset plans, while downside is bounded by balance-sheet capacity and shareholder returns.
financial_review:
**Source hierarchy:** Primary figures from HY26 Appendix 4D interim financial report (`ir_71704f85c242ba81`) and HY26 results presentation (`ir_4613dd281653866c`). **Gap:** No full-year FY25 annual report or audited 10-K equivalent is present in `filings_index.json` (only one filing tagged `annual` is the HY26 presentation, not an annual report). FY22–FY25 annual trends below use **Yahoo `financials_annual.json` fallback**, stated explicitly.

### Interim — H1 FY26 (six months to 31 December 2025)

**Statutory results (Appendix 4D):**

| Metric | H1 FY26 | H1 FY25 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue and other income | $5,527m | $5,610m | -1% |
| EBITA | $295m | $376m | -22% |
| NPATA | $152m | $216m | -30% |
| Statutory EPS | 23.2c | 34.7c | -33% |
| Operating cash flow | $152m | $287m | -47% |

Statutory weakness reflects $82m transformation and business restructuring costs (predominantly Western Europe), excluded from underlying measures.

**Underlying results (Appendix 4D / presentation):**

| Metric | H1 FY26 | H1 FY25 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Aggregated revenue | $6,312m | $5,989m | +5% |
| Underlying EBITA | $377m | $376m | +0.3% |
| Underlying EBITA margin (excl. procurement) | 8.8% | 8.4% | +0.4pp |
| Underlying NPATA | $207m | $216m | -4% |
| Underlying EPS (NPATA basis) | 40.3c | 40.9c | -1% |

Segment trends (presentation): Americas revenue +24% with strong project execution; EMEA flat; **APAC -28%** on professional services completions. Energy +9%, Resources +12%, Chemicals -9%.

**Balance sheet and capital (31 Dec 2025 vs 30 Jun 2025, Appendix 4D):**

- Cash and cash equivalents: **$835m** (down from $952m)
- Net debt (statutory, presentation): **$1,686m** (up from $1,502m at Jun-25)
- Leverage: **1.5x** (target <2.0x)
- Net assets per share: **$10.55** (from $11.00)
- Net tangible liabilities per share: **(0.87)** (from (0.58)) — goodwill/intangibles $5,786m dominate the asset base
- Interest-bearing debt: $1,002m current + $1,526m non-current
- Interim dividend declared: **25c unfranked** (record 5 March 2026; pay 2 April 2026)

Directors’ declaration confirms **going concern** basis and reasonable grounds to pay debts as they fall due. PwC reviewed (not audited) the interim report.

**Cash quality:** Reported operating cash flow fell 47% YoY to $152m; management cites normalized cash conversion of 95.5% after adjusting for advance billing movements. DSO improved to 46.2 days (from 52.0 at FY25).

**Outlook (presentation, forward-looking):** FY26 guidance reconfirmed — higher aggregated revenue growth than FY25, growth in underlying EBITA, underlying EBITA margin ex procurement **9.0–9.5%** (constant currency). Cost-out targeting **$100m+ annualized savings from FY27**.
risks_and_flags:
**Guidance credibility and earnings volatility.** Multiple news items (April–June 2026) report FY26 outlook cuts tied to Middle East project delays and currency, with headlines citing an investor “trust crisis” after a fresh profit warning. Statutory H1 FY26 NPATA fell 30% YoY despite flat underlying EBITA — a wide gap that may unsettle investors relying on statutory numbers.

**Geopolitical and regional concentration.** Middle East disruption is an explicit earnings headwind; EMEA carries legacy Ecuador litigation — civil liability claims of **$195m (US$131m) outstanding** plus tax claims of **$40m (US$26.8m)** per interim notes. Management assesses remote probability of cash outflow, but contingent exposure is material.

**Balance sheet intangibles.** Goodwill of $5,361m and total intangibles $5,786m at 31 Dec 2025 dwarf tangible net assets. Net tangible liabilities per share of (0.87) mean the screen’s P/B ~1.0 reflects goodwill-heavy accounting, not hard asset cover.

**Operational/geographic mix.** APAC revenue down 28% in H1; Chemicals down 9% with Western European project cancellations (low-carbon fuels). Utilization below target at 85.4%; professional services headcount down 8.3% — restructuring risk if demand does not recover.

**FX and translation.** H1 other comprehensive loss of $173m driven largely by foreign currency translation reserve movement (-$171m). Global revenue mix amplifies AUD reporting volatility.

**Debt and covenants.** Leverage 1.5x with net debt rising; weighted average cost of debt 4.4%; interest cover 9.7x — adequate but tightening if earnings disappoint. Bank guarantees outstanding **$1,873m** (up from $1,058m at 30 Jun 2025) increase contingent balance-sheet strain.

**Governance turnover.** Three directors retired between August and November 2025; one appointed — board refresh in progress.

**Pension.** Defined benefit obligations modest at $17m non-current; not a primary red flag.

**Filing gaps.** Absence of indexed FY25 annual report limits verification of full-year contingencies, segment detail and auditor opinion beyond the HY26 review engagement.

research_rationale: Quantitative cheapness and cash-return discipline are supported by filing evidence of flat underlying earnings, strong backlog and balance-sheet headroom, but repeated FY26 guidance downgrades, statutory margin compression and missing full-year primary filings prevent a full confirmation of the screen’s buy signal.
